top_news.title: Goa CM Pramod Sawant says foreign tourist arrivals will return to pre-COVID levels within a year
top_news.summary: Following the disruption caused to tourism worldwide by the COVID-19 pandemic, Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant on Saturday said foreign tourist arrivals in the state were expected to return to pre-COVID levels within a year, while highlighting the government's focus on high-end tourism, infrastructure development, tourist safety and improved transport facilities. In an interview with ANI on foreign tourist arrivals in Goa in 2025, Sawant said, "It is not matching the pre-Covid level yet, but definitely within a year, that will match. I have full faith in this." Highlighting the government's efforts to attract tourists who wish to spend more time in the coastal state, Sawant said the focus was on developing facilities and infrastructure to encourage longer stays. "For those who want to stay longer and spend more time here, it is a high tourist destination that we are targeting. So definitely, facilities like this are also available for them. More and more, their stay will increase. That is why we are trying to increase the stay in the entire state. The good infrastructure that we have created now will increase their stay in Goa," he said. Comparing Goa's tourism strategy with destinations such as Thailand and Vietnam, which are often promoted as affordable holiday options, Sawant said the state was prioritising high-end tourism and witnessing increasing demand for five-star hotels. "That is the marketing strategy for those countries. But definitely, we promote maximum high-end tourism in Goa. For this, the demand for new 5-star hotels in Goa is still increasing. So, I would say that People in India and even in foreign countries, the kind of facilities they get here and the kind of safety they feel, I don't think they will feel so much safety in other countries and other places," the Goa CM added. Addressing negative reports about Goa's roads and cleanliness circulating on social media ahead of the peak tourist season, Sawant alleged that some people were attempting to divert tourism from the state. "Some people target it because they want to divert tourism. I am studying it in depth with the help of the central agencies. Especially with social media, this kind of targeting is always there," he said. He also highlighted the importance of November and December, which see increased tourist activity due to Christmas, the International Film Festival and other celebrations. "November and December are the peak season for Goa. Due to Christmas, the International Film Festival, and many other festivals. People always want to enjoy Goa on the 31st. So most people want to come there. But some people always do negative propaganda like this, especially on social media," Sawant added. On tourist safety, including complaints about high taxi fares and alleged exploitation by taxi operators, Sawant said the state government had deployed additional personnel to assist visitors. "I will say one thing for sure the safety of tourists is important for us. Our Pink Force, an additional tourist force, is working in Goa," he said. Explaining the police response mechanism, the Chief Minister said tourists could contact the police through helpline numbers, adding that personnel were expected to respond within a few minutes. "If someone calls, either on 181, 112, or 100, within 9 minutes, the police are reaching there. Within 5 minutes, within the coastal belt, within 3 to 4 minutes, the police reach there. That is why, for the safety of tourism, we are taking all kinds of precautions." Beyond its beaches, the state is also promoting inland and spiritual tourism, with a focus on temples, churches and other attractions, Sawant said. "That is why, along with the sun, sand, and sea, even though we are promoting spiritual tourism, we are also promoting inland Goa, for the many spiritual temples and churches. We are promoting this now." On public transport connectivity between the airport and tourist destinations, the Goa CM said services had already been introduced through the Kadamba transport system. "We have already started with the public transport system. Now we have the Kadamba transport system, which has started from the airport to the different tourism places," he said, adding that services were available to major tourist destinations at affordable fares. Addressing concerns about taxi availability and fares, Sawant said app-based taxi services were operating in the state and that the government was working to bring more taxi operators under a digital metering system. "We don't have Ola or Uber, but Goa Miles app-based taxis have already started. We are trying to bring the rest of the Goa taxis on the digital meter. The digitalisation of taxis will happen," he said. Referring to complaints about taxi operators charging high fares, he added, "All the tourists come back and say that the taxi operators exploit the situation. Goa Miles is already available, and Goa Digital Taxi is going to start in a few days." Reiterating Goa's tourism strengths in comparison with destinations such as Keralam and Odisha, Sawant said the state was continuing to focus on its natural environment, tourist safety and spiritual attractions. "Definitely, as I said, along with the sun, sand, and sea, one of the best environments is in Goa. And definitely, safety is also important for Goa. The feel of safety in Goa 24 by 7 will not be found in other places. Along with this, we are increasing spiritual tourism," he added. (ANI)

"The meaning of allowing Russia to sell petroleum products was heard loudest right now in Kyiv, when, after numerous uses of jet-powered "Shaheds" against energy facilities, a ballistic missile attack also began. Some of the missiles were successfully shot down," he wrote. Zelenskyy claimed that Russia, through the continued attacks and the new deal with the US, is counting on dragging out the war, inflicting terror upon civilians, and devastating essential infrastructure. He claimed that Moscow will use "every additional billion dollars" earned from petroleum product exports to develop and boost their arsenal and deploy additional mercenaries to the front lines. He asserted that the ongoing conflict will cease only after Russia stops finding any potential in dragging it. "This once again clearly demonstrates what Russia's true intentions are. They are counting on prolonging the war, terror against ordinary people, and the destruction of infrastructure. Every additional billion dollars they can earn from exports, they will spend precisely on this-on sourcing and importing critical components, equipment for weapons production, on enhancing "Shaheds" and manufacturing missiles, and on hiring even more mercenaries for the front lines. Russia's choice is war. And they will only be ready to end it when they sense that the potential to drag it out is diminishing," he added. He called on partners including the US and Europe to support Ukraine and weaken Russia. "Yesterday, unfortunately, there were entirely different signals for Russia-signals that it seems attacks can continue. And this needs to be corrected. articles.title: Goa CM Pramod Sawant says foreign tourist arrivals will return to pre-COVID levels within a year
articles.summary: Following the disruption caused to tourism worldwide by the COVID-19 pandemic, Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant on Saturday said foreign tourist arrivals in the state were expected to return to pre-COVID levels within a year, while highlighting the government's focus on high-end tourism, infrastructure development, tourist safety and improved transport facilities. In an interview with ANI on foreign tourist arrivals in Goa in 2025, Sawant said, "It is not matching the pre-Covid level yet, but definitely within a year, that will match. I have full faith in this." Highlighting the government's efforts to attract tourists who wish to spend more time in the coastal state, Sawant said the focus was on developing facilities and infrastructure to encourage longer stays. "For those who want to stay longer and spend more time here, it is a high tourist destination that we are targeting. So definitely, facilities like this are also available for them. More and more, their stay will increase. That is why we are trying to increase the stay in the entire state. The good infrastructure that we have created now will increase their stay in Goa," he said. Comparing Goa's tourism strategy with destinations such as Thailand and Vietnam, which are often promoted as affordable holiday options, Sawant said the state was prioritising high-end tourism and witnessing increasing demand for five-star hotels. "That is the marketing strategy for those countries. But definitely, we promote maximum high-end tourism in Goa. For this, the demand for new 5-star hotels in Goa is still increasing. So, I would say that People in India and even in foreign countries, the kind of facilities they get here and the kind of safety they feel, I don't think they will feel so much safety in other countries and other places," the Goa CM added. Addressing negative reports about Goa's roads and cleanliness circulating on social media ahead of the peak tourist season, Sawant alleged that some people were attempting to divert tourism from the state. "Some people target it because they want to divert tourism. I am studying it in depth with the help of the central agencies. Especially with social media, this kind of targeting is always there," he said. He also highlighted the importance of November and December, which see increased tourist activity due to Christmas, the International Film Festival and other celebrations. "November and December are the peak season for Goa. Due to Christmas, the International Film Festival, and many other festivals. People always want to enjoy Goa on the 31st. So most people want to come there. But some people always do negative propaganda like this, especially on social media," Sawant added. On tourist safety, including complaints about high taxi fares and alleged exploitation by taxi operators, Sawant said the state government had deployed additional personnel to assist visitors. "I will say one thing for sure the safety of tourists is important for us. Our Pink Force, an additional tourist force, is working in Goa," he said. Explaining the police response mechanism, the Chief Minister said tourists could contact the police through helpline numbers, adding that personnel were expected to respond within a few minutes. "If someone calls, either on 181, 112, or 100, within 9 minutes, the police are reaching there. Within 5 minutes, within the coastal belt, within 3 to 4 minutes, the police reach there. That is why, for the safety of tourism, we are taking all kinds of precautions." Beyond its beaches, the state is also promoting inland and spiritual tourism, with a focus on temples, churches and other attractions, Sawant said. "That is why, along with the sun, sand, and sea, even though we are promoting spiritual tourism, we are also promoting inland Goa, for the many spiritual temples and churches. We are promoting this now." On public transport connectivity between the airport and tourist destinations, the Goa CM said services had already been introduced through the Kadamba transport system. "We have already started with the public transport system. Now we have the Kadamba transport system, which has started from the airport to the different tourism places," he said, adding that services were available to major tourist destinations at affordable fares. Addressing concerns about taxi availability and fares, Sawant said app-based taxi services were operating in the state and that the government was working to bring more taxi operators under a digital metering system. "We don't have Ola or Uber, but Goa Miles app-based taxis have already started. We are trying to bring the rest of the Goa taxis on the digital meter. The digitalisation of taxis will happen," he said. Referring to complaints about taxi operators charging high fares, he added, "All the tourists come back and say that the taxi operators exploit the situation. Goa Miles is already available, and Goa Digital Taxi is going to start in a few days." Reiterating Goa's tourism strengths in comparison with destinations such as Keralam and Odisha, Sawant said the state was continuing to focus on its natural environment, tourist safety and spiritual attractions. "Definitely, as I said, along with the sun, sand, and sea, one of the best environments is in Goa. And definitely, safety is also important for Goa. The feel of safety in Goa 24 by 7 will not be found in other places. Along with this, we are increasing spiritual tourism," he added. (ANI)

articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday expressed disappointment over the US' diesel deal with Russia and asserted that Moscow relies on prolonged warfare, civilian terror, and infrastructure destruction, adding that the relief signals "the attacks can continue." In a post on X, the Ukrainian president voiced criticism of US President Donald Trump's recent annoucement that Russia would immediately supply over 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to American and global markets, pointing to the latest wave of strikes against Ukrainian energy facilities through Russian jet-powered "Shaheds." "The meaning of allowing Russia to sell petroleum products was heard loudest right now in Kyiv, when, after numerous uses of jet-powered "Shaheds" against energy facilities, a ballistic missile attack also began. Some of the missiles were successfully shot down," he wrote. Zelenskyy claimed that Russia, through the continued attacks and the new deal with the US, is counting on dragging out the war, inflicting terror upon civilians, and devastating essential infrastructure. He claimed that Moscow will use "every additional billion dollars" earned from petroleum product exports to develop and boost their arsenal and deploy additional mercenaries to the front lines. He asserted that the ongoing conflict will cease only after Russia stops finding any potential in dragging it. "This once again clearly demonstrates what Russia's true intentions are. They are counting on prolonging the war, terror against ordinary people, and the destruction of infrastructure. Every additional billion dollars they can earn from exports, they will spend precisely on this-on sourcing and importing critical components, equipment for weapons production, on enhancing "Shaheds" and manufacturing missiles, and on hiring even more mercenaries for the front lines. Russia's choice is war. And they will only be ready to end it when they sense that the potential to drag it out is diminishing," he added. Especially criticising the proposed Russian oil and petroleum product supplies deal to the US, Zelenskyy said that it hints at the continuation of strikes rather than an end to the ongoing war. He called on partners including the US and Europe to support Ukraine and weaken Russia. "Yesterday, unfortunately, there were entirely different signals for Russia-signals that it seems attacks can continue. And this needs to be corrected. Strong signals are needed from the United States, from Europe, from other partners. In support of Ukraine and to RESTRICT Russia's ability to wage war and terrorise people. articles.summary: Kerala is set to host a major business and investment gathering as the Brand Keralam Conclave 2026, the fourth edition of the Profit Tusker Summit, takes place on October 15, 2026, at O by Tamara, Thiruvananthapuram. Organized by FYBB and The Profit News, the conclave will bring together business leaders, entrepreneurs, investors, industry experts and key stakeholders to explore strategies for positioning Kerala as a globally competitive destination for business, investment, manufacturing and international trade. The Brand Keralam Conclave 2026 will be inaugurated by Kerala Chief Minister Shri V. D. Satheesan. The prestigious event will also witness the participation of several ministers from the Government of Kerala, alongside prominent business leaders, global investors, entrepreneurs and industry experts. Their participation will add significance to discussions on Kerala's investment opportunities, industrial development, international trade and long-term economic growth. Built around the vision of (Onnamathakanam Keralam) - an aspiration for Kerala to become a leader in economic development and enterprise - the conclave seeks to move beyond conventional business discussions and encourage meaningful dialogue on opportunities that can accelerate the state's economic transformation. With the theme Rooted in Keralam. Ready for the World, the event aims to highlight Kerala's potential to emerge as a significant hub for global investment, entrepreneurship, innovation, exports and maritime commerce. From Business Recognition to Economic Transformation The Profit Tusker platform has steadily evolved into a forum connecting businesses, entrepreneurs and industry leaders from across India. Following three editions held in Kozhikode, Thiruvananthapuram and Kochi, the fourth edition introduces a focused conversation on Kerala's economic future under the Brand Keralam Conclave identity. Unlike traditional business conferences, Brand Keralam Conclave 2026 aims to encourage actionable discussions on investment, infrastructure development, entrepreneurship and industry collaboration. The event will focus on how Kerala can leverage its strategic geographical location, skilled workforce, expanding infrastructure, entrepreneurial ecosystem and international connections to strengthen its position in India's economic growth story.
